conviction_note: The print is very likely a clean beat on profit (revenue is already public at ~2% above the top of guide with FX on the guide's own NT$32 assumption, and the profit consensus is low against it), and the supply chain points to a Q4 guide at or above the +10-15% q/q the street carries. But the last beat-and-raise (Q2, July 2026) was sold on capex and cash flow, the tape is selling AI-capex stories this week (ASML beat and fell after hours), and the 2027 capex/CoWoS questions cut the other way. So the findings sum to +0.2 and p_up is a mild 55 on an abs move of 4.5 (event-implied 3.45-4.3%, scaled up per the repo's record of undersizing), giving +0.45. The two numbers agree in sign and are both small; print_vs_bar is positive (+4%) while the reaction is near a coin flip, which is the reaction function vetoing the fundamental read.
bar: Q3 net profit: LSEG SmartEstimate ~NT$746bn (16 analysts, 12 Oct) and LSEG poll NT$740.8bn (8 Oct), via https://admiralmarkets.com/analytics/traders-blog/tsmc-earnings-q3-2026-preview ; Hudson Labs consensus NI US$22.99bn (~NT$736bn at 32), GM 66.5%, OM 57.1%, revenue US$45.83bn (stale vs actual US$46.7bn) at https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/tsmc-q3-2026-earnings-preview-tsm-revenue-and-margins . Company guide: Q3 rev US$44.6-45.8bn, GM 65-67%, OM 56-58% at USD1=NT$32 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001046179/000104617926000451/a2q26e_withguidancexfinal.htm). Q4 bar: no published consensus number found; BofA and Morgan Stanley both expect +10-15% q/q (https://www.tipranks.com/news/bofa-raises-tsmc-stock-tsm-price-target-ahead-of-q3-earnings-heres-why), and Motley Fool cites analysts at +54% y/y for Q4 (https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/10/14/history-says-this-happens-to-taiwan-semiconductor/), which on Q4 2025's US$33.73bn (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1046179/000104617926000008/a4q25e_withguidancexfinal.htm) is ~US$51.9bn, +11% q/q. The trade turns on the Q4 guide and 2027 commentary, not the Q3 number.
positioning_check: Short interest: Benzinga TSM page (undated, via search snippet, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/TSM/short-interest) shows 30.82M shares short, days to cover 2.76; Curved Trading FINRA settlement 2026-07-15 shows 33.4M, days to cover 2.34 (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/tsm/short-interest/). Not crowded. Skew (baseline) -2.01 vol pts = calls slightly richer than puts ('upside paid'); put/call OI 1.37; ATM IV 53.4%, event-implied move 3.45% (straddle 3.86%). Tape: ADR -8.47% over 5d, +3.47% over 20d, -11% from 52w high (record close US$485.80 on 5 Oct); Taiwan 2330 -1.97% on 13 Oct with foreign investors selling >NT$100bn of Taiwan stocks that day (https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9120507/foreign-selling-pressure-hits-taiwan-stocks-tsmc-tsm-declines).

findings.finding: Q3 revenue is already public at NT$1,494.2bn (~US$46.7bn, implied rate ~NT$32.0 = the guide's own FX assumption), ~3.3% above the guide midpoint and ~2% above its top; the profit consensus (LSEG NT$740.8-746bn, Hudson US$22.99bn ≈ NT$736bn) implies ~50% net margin against Q2's 55.6% and Q1's ~50.5%, while guide-midpoint OM 57% on actual revenue gives NT$741-784bn of net income at the Q1-Q2 net/operating ratios (0.87-0.92), and a GM at the top of range as in Q2 (67.7% vs 65.5-67.5% guide) gives ~NT$767-811bn: a 0-9% profit beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (16 Jul): revenue at top of guide, GM 67.7% above the 65.5-67.5% guide, net profit +77% y/y; ADR fell ~2.9% by 09:44 ET (https://ts2.tech/en/tsmc-nysetsm-tpe2330-stock-drops-on-record-profit-tight-cash-flow/), ~-3.8% per Admirals. The baseline's own 8-row history is monthly 6-Ks, not prints, and is not used.
findings.why_not_priced: The revenue is priced; what may not be is the profit bar, which several estimate sets left near the old revenue guide (Hudson's revenue consensus is still US$45.83bn, below actual). If the beat were priced, previews would carry a consensus GM near 67.5% (only Morgan Stanley does; Hudson 66.5%, BofA 67.0%) and a net profit near NT$780bn rather than 746bn.
findings.independence: Q2/Q1 actuals and the Q3 guide from TSMC's own 6-Ks (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001046179/000104617926000451/a2q26e_withguidancexfinal.htm, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1046179/000104617926000199/a1q26e_withguidancexfinal.htm); September revenue from TSMC's release (https://pr.tsmc.com/english/news/3343). The arithmetic is mine from those documents.

findings.finding: Counterparty and supply-chain data since TSMC's July call point to a Q4 guide at or above the street's +10-15% q/q (~US$51.9bn): Foxconn's September revenue was NT$1.1586tn (+38% y/y, +25.7% m/m, first month above NT$1tn), Q3 +47% y/y, with Vera Rubin racks in mass production in Q3 and AI operations 'expected to continue growing in the fourth quarter' (5 Oct); TrendForce (3 Aug) had TSMC 3nm wafer starts reaching 180K/month by early 4Q26, 2-3 months ahead of plan; and TSMC has landed at or above the top of its revenue guide three quarters running (Q1 35.9 vs 34.6-35.8, Q2 40.2 vs 39.0-40.2, Q3 46.7 vs 44.6-45.8).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 2025 print (15 Jan 2026): Q1 guide US$34.6-35.8bn plus a US$52-56bn capex surprise; ADR up ~4-5% pre-market (https://www.hl.co.uk/shares/stock-market-news/company--news/shares-jump-as-tsmc-posts-record-q4-numbers). Q2 2026: Q3 guide +12% q/q at midpoint and 2026 growth raised to 'slightly above 40%', stock still fell ~3-4% on capex/FCF.
findings.why_not_priced: The ADR fell 8.5% in five sessions on AI-funding fear (Hock Tan's capital comment, the FT OpenAI run-rate story, the CXMT memory scare), none of it TSMC-specific, while sell-side Q4 estimates still sit at +10-15%. If the market were pricing a guide above the range, the stock would not be -11% from its 5 Oct high going into the print; the skew (-2.01, calls paid) does lean the same way, so part of it is in.
findings.independence: TrendForce 3nm wafer starts (https://www.trendforce.com/news/2026/08/03/news-tsmc-3nm-monthly-wafer-starts-to-hit-180k-by-early-4q26-on-strong-demand-2-3-months-ahead-of-expectations/); guide-vs-actual from TSMC 6-Ks (Q1: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1046179/000104617926000199/a1q26e_withguidancexfinal.htm; Q2/Q3 guide: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001046179/000104617926000451/a2q26e_withguidancexfinal.htm). Foxconn and TrendForce are proxies, not TSMC's own Q4 number.

findings.finding: Reports that TSMC has set 2027 wafer price increases (Nikkei: customers including Apple, Nvidia and AMD formally notified of 5-10% across advanced and mature nodes; DigiTimes 24 Sep: 3-6% from January 2027, larger on the most advanced nodes); Morgan Stanley (6 Oct) models 2027 GM close to 70% on +5-10% pricing. Management confirming hikes or a structurally higher margin on the call would firm the 2027 bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No sourced earnings-day reaction to a TSMC pricing confirmation found. TSMC typically declines to comment on pricing specifics on calls.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the hikes are in every preview and in the MS/BofA models. What is not settled is the size (3-6% vs 5-10%); a company confirmation at the high end is the only unpriced part.
findings.independence: Nikkei account summarised in https://www.benzinga.com/markets/tech/26/09/61964879/tsmc-reportedly-plans-to-hike-wafer-price-next-year ; BofA expects 5-10% advanced-node hikes in Q1 2027 (https://www.tipranks.com/news/bofa-raises-tsmc-stock-tsm-price-target-ahead-of-q3-earnings-heres-why).

findings.finding: Capex is the line this stock was sold on last time and the tape is selling AI-capex stories now: in July the 2026 capex raise to US$60-64bn with FCF conversion falling to 40.7% from 60.8% took the ADR down ~3% on a beat; street 2027 capex expectations now run US$75-83bn (MS 75-80, Citi 77, BofA 83), ASML guided Q4 sales to EUR14.2-15.2bn (vs EUR11.7bn in Q3) and said 2027-28 supply will not meet customer demand, and any 2027 capex signal at or above that range lands in a week when Broadcom's CEO called capital the biggest AI constraint (12 Oct).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (16 Jul): capex raise + weaker FCF conversion -> ADR -2.9% early, ~-3.8% on the day per Admirals. Q4 2025 (15 Jan 2026): a larger-than-expected capex guide was bought (+4-5% pre-market). So the sign of this line depends on the tape, and this week's tape is AI-funding fear.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock is already -8.5% over 5 days on the same fear. What is not priced is the specific number: TSMC normally gives the next-year capex range in January, so an October hint of 2027 'meaningfully higher' with FCF pressure would be fresh. If the market had fully priced it, the skew would be put-leaning, and it is call-leaning.
findings.independence: ASML Q3 release (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/10/14/3380319/0/en/asml-reports-11-7-billion-total-net-sales-and-5-0-billion-net-income-in-q3-2026.html); street 2027 capex figures (https://admiralmarkets.com/analytics/traders-blog/tsmc-earnings-q3-2026-preview, https://www.tipranks.com/news/bofa-raises-tsmc-stock-tsm-price-target-ahead-of-q3-earnings-heres-why); Hock Tan (https://www.thestar.com.my/tech/tech-news/2026/10/12/broadcom-ceo-says-biggest-hurdle-in-ai-fuelled-tech-growth-is-capital-not-memory-chips).

findings.finding: DigiTimes (1 Sep) reported TSMC pushed back placing its 2027 advanced-packaging (CoWoS) equipment orders, prompting speculation about excess CoWoS capacity ahead; suppliers said demand has not weakened and the delay reflects the CoWoS-to-CoPoS reallocation. It is a question management will be asked, and an answer pointing to slower CoWoS growth would hit the AI-demand narrative.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No sourced earnings-day reaction on CoWoS commentary specifically.
findings.why_not_priced: It is six weeks old and was contested by the suppliers themselves; previews do not mention it. If it were priced, CoWoS capacity estimates in previews would have come down; MS still carries 130K/200K/260K per month for 2026/27/28.
findings.independence: TrendForce (14 Sep) says TSMC targets CoWoS to double by 2028 (https://www.trendforce.com/news/2026/09/14/news-tsmc-reportedly-targets-22-2nm-16-3nm-capacity-boost-by-mid-2027-cowos-to-double-by-2028), which points the other way; the finding is sized net of it.

findings.finding: The 8.5% five-day drawdown into the print came from sector events, not TSMC news: the CXMT DRAM claim (SK Hynix -10%, KOSPI -5.5% on 13 Oct; TSMC makes no DRAM), the FT's report of OpenAI's run-rate near US$50bn (SOX -3.4% on 8 Oct), Hock Tan's 'capital is the constraint', and record foreign selling in Taiwan. The call is the first company voice on AI demand since; a reaffirmation that demand stays tight through 2028-30 meets a de-risked tape, and the option market already leans upside (skew -2.01).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No sourced case of TSM reacting to a demand reaffirmation after a sector drawdown; Q4 2025 (Jan 2026, after an AI-bubble scare) was bought ~4-5%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the skew and the run-up both say the market expects some relief. What is not priced is how far a TSMC-specific number moves a stock that fell on others' news; the -11% from the high is what a market NOT pricing relief looks like.
findings.independence: Yahoo, 13 Oct, on the CXMT sympathy move (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/tsmc-stock-falls-2-days-063902629.html); Euronews on the OpenAI story (https://euronews.com/2026/10/09/what-happened-to-openais-20bn-revenue-scare-rattles-ai-trade); foreign selling (https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9120507/foreign-selling-pressure-hits-taiwan-stocks-tsmc-tsm-declines).

findings.finding: The nearest peer print sold its beat: ASML reported record Q3 sales EUR11.7bn, 57.5% GM, EPS well above consensus and a strong Q4 guide (EUR14.2-15.2bn) on 14 Oct and its ADR fell a further 2.26% after hours to US$1,679 after -1.86% in the session, read as strength already priced. This is evidence of the reaction function in the semis tape this week.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: TSM's own last print (Q2 2026) was a beat sold ~3-4%.
findings.why_not_priced: It happened within the last session; ASML's regular-session reaction on 14 Oct was not found, so how much of this the TSM close already holds is unknown. If the market had fully digested it, TSM's -2.8% intraday on 14 Oct would be the whole of it.
findings.independence: Shares a theme (semis selling beats) with the capex finding but rests on a different document (ASML's tape, not TSMC's capex). The ASML release itself is bullish on demand (https://www.stocktitan.net/articles/asml-q3-2026-earnings-ai-chip-machine-demand), which offsets part of this.

baseline_tension: The evidence agrees with the call-leaning skew (-2.01) and cuts against the 5-day run-up (-8.47%) as a statement about TSMC's own numbers, but the last print sold a beat on capex and the peer (ASML) sold a beat the night before, so the positive lean is kept small (p_up 55, not 60).
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction; Q2 beat was sold): Q3 profit-beat finding cut from +0.6 to +0.3; p_up from 57 to 55
Lesson 5 (proxies smaller): Q4-guide finding resting on Foxconn/TrendForce cut from +0.8 to +0.6
Lesson 3/7 (caveat reaches the number; agreeing with the skew means partly priced): 2027 pricing finding +0.3 -> +0.2 and positioning-relief finding +0.4 -> +0.3
Lesson 7: short interest checked before the negatives (DTC 2.3-2.8, not crowded); negatives left at size
Lesson 6: bar sourced to two agreeing LSEG sets plus Hudson for Q3, and BofA+MS for Q4; no cap needed
Rebuilt base rate from confirmed prints per the 'wrong events' lesson; abs_move 4.5 unchanged
